title: Good productivity app if you know what you’re doing.
body:
ToDoist is a great app for people who know how and why to organise tasks and projects. Do not expect the app to do the work for you, this app will not decide your priorities, will not make you meet deadlines and will not work for you unless you put the work in yourself. 

That being said, if you know what and how you should be managing your ‘to do list’ this app is absolutely amazing. After reading Getting Things Done by David Allen this app made my head and agenda so much clearer. It allows me to put all the things that pop up in my head in the app so that I don’t have to keep remembering everything all the time. In daily life I am a student Electrical Engineering, active member of a student and study association, Vice President of a student recruitment committee and presenter at a small firm. Keeping my head clear and being able to focus on one thing at a time is key to managing all my responsibilities and tasks. Without ToDoist, I don’t think I would have been able to manage everything at the same time. Love the app.

title: Almost as perfect as Wunderlist
body:
After trying out so many other todo-systems in replacement of Wunderlist, that will be gone soon, I have finally found something almost as good.

I love that all the projects and task can be imported from Wunderlist with one simple click. It also has almost the same layout what makes it familiar. Todoist provides more options prioritise your projects and tasks.

Todoist sure beats Wunderlist’ follow up ToDo from Microsoft.

What would make Todoist even better is, if subtasks not only could be moved from one project to another, but also be moved on taks level, so from one task to another task in the same or another project.

Second what would be a great help, if you could choose multiple options to prioritise your projects and tasks, like first date, second priority, then name or whatever order you prefer for example.

I hope this features will be introduced in the nearby future. And, if possible, nice background options from stock or your own pictures would personalise it and make use of Todoist even more fun.

title: Intuitive & minimalistic excellent tool
body:
Great tool which declutters and provides overview. Karma point & daily targets help you get a better feeling how you’re doing. 

For a while I tried writing down everything in a bullet journal on a daily basis, but in the end it doesn’t work fast enough and you don’t carry it on the go, whereas the app is present on all my computers/phones.

Great customization and ability to add single tasks as well as complex projects. Only possible improvements are: 2-way sync with calendars (now only Google) and more options to estimate the size of a task (eg by time needed or with Fibonacci numers) and some kind of agile overview (so you know what is started and what task are waiting for that task to be completed).

Ik heb het al eerder aangekaart, de ontwikkelaars bleken zich er al bewust van te zijn. We zijn inmiddels zeker 5 app updates verder (waarschijnlijk al 10), maar aan dit probleem is nog helemaal niks gedaan.

title: Multiple sync platforms only reason I stay with Todoist

The layout for Todoist is quite messy, especially in the ipad-version. Comparing with other todo-apps I miss things like making tasks disappear when they are not due, paring subtasks in an easy way to their parents, arranging the sequence of tags and filtering by project. 
A lot of the things I miss can be done, but it requires complex and cumbersome workarounds.
Also there are several little strange flaws like tasks become invisible when I use certain keybord icons or the sequence of tasks, projects or tags changes for unknown reasons.

The only reason that untill now I stay with Todoist is the multiple sync platforms in combination with the possibility to attach documents.

author: AlteKiet

title: Nice to-do list
body:
This is a nice app that lets you organise your tasks into projects containing individual items or sub-projects.It's refreshingly simple: no graphics or superfluous agendas here.  It uses your e-mail address heavily to remind you of your present and overdue tasks.
It would be helpful if it not only reminded you that a task is overdue, but also which task. It syncs well with the Todoist website on your computer.

Despite some shortcomings I recommend this straightforward and uncluttered app. I will continue using it and probably upgrade to the paid (Premium) version that promises several interesting extras.
